sentences.zh: 戶一千四百萬二千七百六十。

translations.literal: Households numbered fourteen million two thousand seven hundred sixty.
translations.idiomatic: Households numbered 14,002,760.

sentences.zh: 賜皇后、親王、公主如歲例。

translations.literal: The empress, imperial princes, and princesses were granted gifts as in the annual precedent.
translations.idiomatic: The empress, imperial princes, and princesses were granted gifts as in the annual precedent.

sentences.zh: 賜諸臣羊馬價，鈔四十三萬四千五百錠、幣五萬五千四百一十錠。

translations.literal: Sheep and horse prices were granted to various ministers — four hundred thirty-four thousand five hundred ingots of notes and fifty-five thousand four hundred ten ingots of silks.
translations.idiomatic: Sheep and horse prices were granted to various ministers — 434,500 ingots of notes and 55,410 ingots of silks.

sentences.zh: 周貧乏，鈔三萬七千五百二十錠。

translations.literal: To relieve the poor, thirty-seven thousand five hundred twenty ingots of notes were granted.
translations.idiomatic: To relieve the poor, 37,520 ingots of notes were granted.

sentences.zh: 作佛事祈福五十一。

translations.literal: Fifty-one Buddhist rites for blessing were performed.
translations.idiomatic: 51 Buddhist rites for blessing were performed.

sentences.zh: 真定、寧晉等處，被水、旱、蝗、雹為災者二十九。

translations.literal: Twenty-nine places including Zhending and Ningjin suffered disasters of flood, drought, locusts, or hail.
translations.idiomatic: 29 places including Zhending and Ningjin suffered disasters of flood, drought, locusts, or hail.

sentences.zh: 斷死罪四十。

translations.literal: Forty persons were sentenced to death.
translations.idiomatic: 40 persons were sentenced to death.

sentences.zh: 三十一年春正月壬子朔，帝不豫，免朝賀。

translations.literal: Thirty-first year, spring, first month, on the renzi new moon, the Emperor was unwell and court congratulations were waived.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-first year, on the renzi new moon of the first month of spring, the Emperor was unwell and court congratulations were waived.

sentences.zh: 癸亥，知樞密院事伯顏至自軍中。

translations.literal: On guihai day Bayan, overseer of the Privy Council, arrived from the army.
translations.idiomatic: On guihai day Bayan, overseer of the privy council, arrived from the army.

sentences.zh: 庚午，帝大漸。

translations.literal: On gengwu day the Emperor grew gravely ill.
translations.idiomatic: On gengwu day the Emperor grew gravely ill.

sentences.zh: 癸酉，帝崩於紫檀殿。

translations.literal: On guiyou day the Emperor died in the Zitan Hall.
translations.idiomatic: On guiyou day the Emperor died in the Zitan Hall.

sentences.zh: 在位三十五年，壽八十。

translations.literal: He had reigned thirty-five years and lived to eighty.
translations.idiomatic: He had reigned 35 years and lived to 80.

sentences.zh: 親王、諸大臣發使告哀於皇孫。

translations.literal: Princes and major ministers dispatched envoys to announce mourning to the imperial grandson.
translations.idiomatic: Princes and major ministers dispatched envoys to announce mourning to the imperial grandson.

sentences.zh: 乙亥，靈駕發引，葬起輦谷，從諸帝陵。

translations.literal: On yihai day the imperial bier set out; he was buried at Qilian Valley, following the imperial tombs.
translations.idiomatic: On yihai day the imperial bier set out; he was buried at Qilian Valley, following the imperial tombs.

sentences.zh: 夏四月，皇孫至上都。

translations.literal: Summer, fourth month, the imperial grandson arrived at Shangdu.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of summer, the imperial grandson arrived at Shangdu.

sentences.zh: 甲午，即皇帝位。

translations.literal: On jiawu day he ascended the imperial throne.
translations.idiomatic: On jiawu day he ascended the imperial throne.

sentences.zh: 丙午，中書右丞相完澤及文武百官議上尊謚。

translations.literal: On bingwu day Right Chancellor of the Central Secretariat Wanze and the civil and military officials deliberated on conferring a posthumous honorific title.
translations.idiomatic: On bingwu day Right Chancellor of the central secretariat Wanze and the civil and military officials deliberated on conferring a posthumous honorific title.

sentences.zh: 壬寅，始為壇於都城南七里。

translations.literal: On renyin day an altar was first established seven li south of the capital.
translations.idiomatic: On renyin day an altar was first established seven li south of the capital.

sentences.zh: 甲辰，遣司徒兀都帶、平章政事不忽木、左丞張九思，率百官請謚於南郊。

translations.literal: On jiachen day Grand Preceptor Udutai, Grand Councillor Buqumu, and Left Associate Administrator Zhang Jiusi were dispatched to lead all officials in requesting a posthumous title at the Southern Suburb.
translations.idiomatic: On jiachen day Grand Preceptor Udutai, Grand Councillor Buqumu, and Left Associate Administrator Zhang Jiusi were dispatched to lead all officials in requesting a posthumous title at the Southern Suburb.

sentences.zh: 五月戊午，遣攝太尉臣兀都帶奉冊上尊謚曰聖德神功文武皇帝，廟號世祖，國語尊稱曰薛禪皇帝。

translations.literal: Fifth month, on wuwu day Acting Grand Preceptor Udutai was dispatched to present the register and confer the honorific title Emperor Sacred in Virtue, Divine in Achievement, Martial and Civil; the temple name was Shizu, and in the national language he was styled Emperor Setsen.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, on wuwu day Acting Grand Preceptor Udutai was dispatched to present the register and confer the honorific title Emperor Sacred in Virtue, Divine in Achievement, Martial and Civil; the temple name was Shizu, and in the national language he was styled Emperor Setsen.

sentences.zh: 是日，完澤等議同上先皇后弘吉剌氏尊謚曰昭睿順聖皇后。

translations.literal: That day Wanze and others likewise deliberated and conferred on the late empress of the Onggirat clan the honorific title Empress Zhaorui Shunsheng.
translations.idiomatic: That day Wanze and others likewise deliberated and conferred on the late empress of the Onggirat clan the honorific title Empress Zhaorui Shunsheng.

sentences.zh: 世祖度量弘廣，知人善任使，信用儒術，用能以夏變夷，立經陳紀，所以為一代之制者，規模宏遠矣。

translations.literal: Shizu was broad in measure, knew men and employed them well, trusted Confucian learning, and by these means was able to transform the barbarians through Chinese ways; in establishing classics and setting forth regulations, the institutions of his age were grand and far-reaching.
translations.idiomatic: Shizu was magnanimous in spirit, knew men and employed them well, trusted Confucian learning, and thereby transformed the barbarians through Chinese ways; the institutions he established for his age were grand and far-reaching.
